title: Anomalous Attrition Rate Among Cleared Aerospace-Nuclear Personnel Triggers Federal Counterintelligence Review
finding: Deaths and disappearances among cleared aerospace-nuclear personnel cluster geographically and temporally at a rate exceeding baseline, exposing a multi-year detection gap in personnel-security monitoring
forecast: The FBI review will identify procedural gaps in continuous-evaluation programs but will not establish a single connective thread across all 11 cases by end of 2026

title: Pre-Testimony Deaths of Individuals With Knowledge of Classified Retrieval Programs Indicate Potential Program-Protection Activity
finding: Three individuals who agreed to testify before legislative bodies about classified aerospace-retrieval programs died before delivering testimony, a temporal correlation indicating either program-protection tradecraft or a chilling effect producing equivalent outcomes
forecast: No additional pre-testimony deaths will occur through 2027 as scrutiny intensity has raised the cost-benefit calculus; suppression will shift to legal and administrative channels

title: Cross-Era Recurrence of Anomalous Scientist Attrition in Defense-Adjacent Programs Suggests Structural Phenomenon
finding: Anomalous clusters of deaths among scientists working on classified defense programs have recurred across at least three eras — 1949-Cold War, 1982-1990 Britain, 2021-2026 US — indicating a structural feature of sensitive-technology program management
forecast: Similar attrition clusters will recur in the next major technology transition involving sharp classification boundaries, likely in directed-energy or quantum-computing programs, within the next decade

title: Foreign Intelligence Targeting of Cleared Scientific Personnel Operates Through Recruitment Not Elimination
finding: Documented foreign intelligence operations against cleared US aerospace-nuclear personnel use recruitment and infiltration, not physical elimination — a tradecraft profile that does not match the current attrition pattern, narrowing the plausible actor set
forecast: Foreign recruitment operations against cleared US scientific personnel will intensify through 2027 as institutional instability continues, regardless of the attrition-investigation outcome
